rounds.name: Presentation Glitch
rounds.situation: Your group’s presentation file won’t open. You present in five minutes. One person still has the outline, and another has the pictures.
rounds.discussion: What could your group do with the outline and pictures? How does your finished line help?

rounds.name: The Paper Bridge
rounds.situation: Your group’s paper bridge bends under the first weight. The judges arrive in ten minutes. You have spare paper and tape.
rounds.discussion: What does your ending suggest the group do with the ten minutes they have left?
rounds.wordHint: A stitch is a loop of thread that holds pieces of fabric together.
rounds.traditionalMeaning: Fix a small problem early so it takes less work to solve.

rounds.name: Credit for the Comic
rounds.opener: The hardest part of working together is …
rounds.situation: You and a friend made a comic. The school puts it on display. At lunch, everyone starts telling your friend how good their comic is. Nobody knows you helped.
rounds.discussion: How would your ending help you decide what to say to your friend?

rounds.name: The Rained-Out Fair
rounds.opener: Attention, everyone. There’s been a change. …
rounds.situation: Rain starts just before the outdoor school fair. The tables are getting wet. You have one minute to tell everyone what’s happening. The gym is open.
rounds.discussion: If people heard your announcement, what would they know or do next? Which detail might they still need?

rounds.name: Just Before the Lights
rounds.opener: I took a deep breath and said, “…”
rounds.situation: It’s dress rehearsal. You are about to walk onstage when the lights go out. A younger student next to you quietly says, “I’m scared.”
rounds.discussion: How would the younger student react if they heard your line? Which detail in the scene makes you think that?
